main_html:
Educational Guides

How USCIS Medical Exams Are Typically Completed and Verified

Independent, educational frameworks explaining how USCIS medical exams (Form I-693) are typically completed, what documents matter, and what applicants commonly misunderstand. Not legal advice. No endorsements or rankings.

Quick answer: These guides explain process flow and document readiness — not whether you should choose any specific civil surgeon.

When this page helps most: when you still need to decide which guide matches the actual question before you compare options or contact anyone.

Common mistake: staying on the hub too long when the real answer lives in a comparison, costs, red-flags, or questions-to-ask guide.

%%AD:global_guides_top%%

How to use these guides well

Each guide walks through a key part of the I-693 process: what to bring, what to ask, typical timeframes and costs, and what to do after the exam. Start with the guide that matches where you are in the process.

guide_cards.title: USCIS Medical Exam Cost
guide_cards.description: USCIS charges nothing to file Form I-693. The civil surgeon sets the exam fee and it is published nowhere. Here are the fees that are published, from the current USCIS fee schedule.

guide_cards.title: N-648 Medical Waiver
guide_cards.description: Form N-648 asks USCIS to excuse the English and civics requirements for naturalization on medical grounds. USCIS charges nothing to file it. The medical professional may charge.

guide_cards.title: USCIS Interview Checklist
guide_cards.description: A preparation checklist for a USCIS interview, covering the documents to bring, the medical exam validity question, and the fees that are published for the underlying application.

guide_cards.title: N-400 Checklist
guide_cards.description: What USCIS itself lists on the Form N-400 checklist of required initial evidence, what the fee is, and the translation rule that catches people out.

guide_cards.title: Citizenship Test
guide_cards.description: Two naturalization civics tests are in use at the same time. Which one you sit is decided by when USCIS received your Form N-400, and the two are not the same size.

guide_cards.title: Naturalization Test Exemptions
guide_cards.description: Age and years as a permanent resident can excuse the English requirement but not the civics test. A medical condition can excuse both.

guide_cards.title: I-693 Form Instructions
guide_cards.description: The rule everyone repeats is never open the sealed envelope. USCIS now instructs online I-485 filers to do exactly that.
